name: Lancet Loitering Munition

cost.display: ~$35,000 per unit (export listing cites ~3M RUB / ~$37,000 for Lancet-3)

short_role: Catapult-launched loitering munition used for combined reconnaissance and precision strike against vehicles, artillery, and personnel near the line.
characteristics: Warhead: ~1 kg (Lancet-1) or ~3 kg (Lancet-3), HE, HE-fragmentation, or shaped-charge variants
Terminal guidance via onboard optical seeker, often cued by a separate reconnaissance UAV
employment_notes: Typically operates as a hunter-killer pair with a separate ISR drone (e.g. a Zala or Orlan-type reconnaissance UAV) that finds and confirms the target before the Lancet is committed — the strike asset itself carries little independent search capability.
contrast_vs_traditional: This collapses what used to be a multi-step, multi-hour kill chain (spot target → report → request fires → wait for artillery/air) into a single-digit-minutes engagement run by a small crew, without committing a manned aircraft or a full artillery battery. It also pushes both sides' vehicles and artillery further from the line and toward constant movement/camouflage discipline, since a static asset within the drone's radius is now findable and killable within minutes.

reactive_behavior.description: On select: drone loiters, dives on a target, brief impact vignette.

connections.description: Cued onto targets by a paired reconnaissance UAV feed.
Airframes and batteries resupplied from a near-rear logistics point.
Receives target designation from a squad-level fire-control terminal.
